title: Sudan Black Staining of Zebrafish Larvae
author: Emily Rosowski
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.rced2te
materials: Cover in aluminum foil, rock at 4°C overnight.

steps.title: Prepare and Fix Larvae
steps.instruction: Anesthetize zebrafish larvae and fix them using formaldehyde.

substeps.instruction: Transfer larvae to 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tubes.
Prepare fresh 4% formaldehyde in PBS by mixing 1 ml 16% formaldehyde, 400 μl 10x PBS, and 2.6 ml H2O.
Pipet off as much liquid as possible from the tubes.
Cover tubes in aluminum foil and rock at 4°C overnight.

steps.title: Stain with Sudan Black B
steps.instruction: Wash the fixed larvae and apply Sudan Black B stain.

substeps.instruction: Wash larvae in 1 ml 1x PBS for >5 min, rocking at 4°C; repeat for a total of 3 washes.
Pipet off as much PBS as possible.
Add 1 ml working solution of Sudan Black B.
Cover in aluminum foil and rock at RT for 1 hour.

steps.title: Wash and Depigment Larvae
steps.instruction: Remove pigment from larvae while preserving the Sudan Black signal.

substeps.instruction: Wash larvae in 1 ml 70% ethanol for 5 min, rocking at RT; repeat for a total of 3 washes.
Rehydrate larvae by washing in PBS-Tween for 5 min, rocking at RT.
Pipet off as much PBS-Tween as possible.
Add 1 ml Depigmentation solution (composed of 400 μl 10% KOH, 133 μl 30% H2O2, and 3.467 ml H2O).
Verify depigmentation under a zoomscope to ensure pigment is mostly lost but Sudan Black signal remains.

steps.title: Final Wash and Storage
steps.instruction: Perform final washes and store the larvae.

substeps.instruction: Wash larvae in 1 ml PBS-Tween for 5 min, rocking at RT; repeat for a total of 2 washes.
For longer-term storage, change the liquid to 1x PBS (no Tween).
